subject: Audit log granularity map & export checklist for SOC2 vendor review
messages:
From: Audit Team <audit-team@horizon-audit.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: Audit log granularity map & export checklist for SOC2 vendor review

Hi Priyom,

I'm on the Horizon Health SOC2 engagement and my lead asked for more detail about the shape and exportability of Redwood's admin/activity logs for evidence. Specifically we need:

- An enumerated fieldset (event_type, actor_id, actor_role, target_id, target_type, timestamp_utc, request_id, region, ip, action_result, kv_cache_op_tag, session_id, trace_id, model_variant)
- Which fields are PII and what redaction options exist for exports
- Typical retention windows by event class (operator actions, system events, ephemeral KV cache entries)
- Export formats you support (NDJSON, Parquet, compressed tar) and example manifests/checksums
- How exports are attested: signed manifests, HMAC, or notarized delivery (we need chain-of-custody language)
- Whether streaming audit feeds are available (Kafka / pubsub) vs on-demand batch bundles

Can you send a short checklist + a sample export manifest we can attach to the audit working papers? A small sampled file (no real customer data) that shows the fieldset/headers would be perfect.

Thanks,
Ben Ortiz
Senior Auditor — Horizon Health
ben.ortiz@horizon-audit.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
To: Audit Team <audit-team@horizon-audit.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Dec 2025 13:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Audit log granularity map & export checklist for SOC2 vendor review

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a small, synthetic sample and a CSV field-map that maps our internal event classes to the requested fields. Quick answers below and an export checklist at the end.

High-level:
- Fieldset: we can produce the exact header list you requested. Our canonical export includes event_type, ts_utc, request_id, actor_id (internal id), actor_email (if requested), actor_role, target_id, target_type, action, result_code, ip_addr, region, trace_id, session_id, model_name, model_variant, kv_op (for operator KV/cache ops), and delta_payload_size_bytes. See attached audit-log-fieldset.csv for column descriptions and enumerated values for event_type and action.

- PII & redaction: actor_email and ip_addr are considered sensitive. We support these redaction options at export time: none (full), pseudonymize (hash actor_email using HMAC-SHA256 with customer key), or redact (empty). We do not include full prompt text in admin-activity exports by default; prompts are separate telemetry and handled under a different evidence request.

- Retention windows:
  - Privileged operator actions (role=operator/admin): default 5 years (adjustable per contract); hot indexes maintained for 90 days.
  - System operational events (scheduler, autoscaler, infra): 1 year by default.
  - KV/cache routing events and ephemeral cache keys: 90 days; we can provide a delta-only sampling for longer windows.
  - Sessionization traces and request-level traces (trace_id): 180 days.

- Export formats & signing: supported exports: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Apache Parquet, gzipped CSV. Bundles are delivered as sha256-signed tar.gz with an export-manifest-checksum.txt (HMAC-SHA256) and an attached signed manifest (PKCS7) if required for legal attestation. We also support direct S3 PUT to a customer-bucket with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and an accompanying signed manifest.

- Streaming: we support a read-only Kafka topic for on-demand streaming (retention per topic based on contract), or periodic batch bundles. For SOC2 evidence we typically provide batched, attested bundles with manifest + checksum to keep chain-of-custody clear.

Export checklist (short):
1) Confirm event classes and date window (e.g., privileged ops 2024-01-01 -> 2025-11-30)
2) Confirm PII handling policy (none / pseudonymize / redact)
3) Choose format (NDJSON recommended for sampling + easy review)
4) Delivery method (S3 presigned, SFTP, or secure Drive link)
5) Decide on manifest attestation (simple HMAC vs PKCS7 signed manifest)
6) Approve timeline (sample within 48 hours; full bundle depends on window size — estimate provided after scope)

Attachments included: audit-log-fieldset.csv (column map), sample-ndjson-20251130.ndjson (synthetic rows), export-manifest-checksum.txt (example).

Action: if you confirm PII handling and window, I'll kick off a sample export and we can iterate.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.example.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Audit Team <audit-team@horizon-audit.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Audit log granularity map & export checklist for SOC2 vendor review

On Mon, Dec 1, 2025 at 13:04 +0000, Priyom Das wrote:
> Attachments included: audit-log-fieldset.csv (column map), sample-ndjson-20251130.ndjson (synthetic rows), export-manifest-checksum.txt (example).

Quick internal note and a small ask for Ben: please confirm whether Horizon wants operator identity mapped to human-readable directory (email) in the export, or if hashed operator ids suffice for your paper trail. Hashing is our default for cross-tenant exports; we can provide a separate mapping file under NDAs to link internal operator_id -> email for audit teams. Also, include the following fields in the sample export if possible:

- kv_op_tag (to show cache invalidation vs cache-populate events)
- op_privilege_level (0/1/2) so reviewers can filter privileged commands
- sessionized_user_anon_id (for session-level aggregation)

If Ben confirms, I'll update the sample and sign off on manifest format (PKCS7) before Priyom publishes the bundle. Timeline: sample updated within 24 hrs after confirmation; full export ETA depends on window (we typically run a 72-hr job for ~18 months of events).

Thanks —Karthik
Director, Production Security

From: Audit Team <audit-team@horizon-audit.com>

Thanks — that level of detail is great. For the Horizon engagement: we want pseudonymized operator emails (HMAC) in the sample and the mapping file under NDA; NDJSON is fine; please include the kv_op_tag and op_privilege_level columns. We'll take PKCS7 signed manifests. Can you send the sample and manifest link once ready?

Ben
